headline: Sort starts so overlaps form one continuous run
statement: Given closed intervals [start,end], merge every overlapping group and return the resulting non-overlapping intervals covering exactly the same points. Touching endpoints overlap. Return the resulting intervals in any order.
intuition: Sort intervals by their starting point. Then compare each interval with the last range you have saved. If they overlap, extend that saved range. Otherwise, begin a new range. Sorting means the next interval cannot overlap an earlier saved range without also reaching the last one.
approach: Append the first interval. For each later interval, compare its start with the latest merged end.
If start <= end, extend the end to their maximum. Otherwise append a new interval.
correctness: The merged list is a disjoint sorted cover of the processed prefix. Because the next start is at least all preceding starts, it cannot overlap any component except the last. Extending that component or appending a new one preserves the invariant. At termination the list is exactly the input union.
bruteForce: Repeatedly inspect every pair and merge overlaps until none remain; repeated rescans can be quadratic or worse.

complexity.explanation: Sorting uses O(n log n); the sweep and returned intervals use O(n).

pitfalls: Closed intervals touching at one point merge.
Nested intervals must not shrink the current end.
Copy intervals rather than unexpectedly altering input rows.
